title.narrative: Pathway to Sustainable, Resilient and Inclusive development in Jajpur, Vyasanagar and Panasa Gram Panchayat in Odisha, India - Phase 1 and 2

description.narrative:
Phase 1: The potential for higher urbanization rate in the near future presents an immense opportunity for core urban centers in the Jajpur district and Panasa GP to benefit from the social and economic growth rendered by regional development. Given its location and natural assets, Jajpur, Vyasanagar and Panasa GP have several key resources which if harnessed and managed strategically, can offer a green growth dividend for long term economic prosperity and ecological sustainability.
To achieve the above and carve out a path of sustainable urbanization with economic prosperity, the twin cities and Panasa GP need to have a spatial strategic plan that is evidence-based and have a strong monitoring framework for performance of its development trajectory. The development sectors are interconnected with each other and therefore require an integrated and holistic approach for sustainability. Development policies, spatial plans, and strategic actions and interventions must be grounded in low-carbon and climate resilient approach combined with technological innovations to put the region on the path to transformative urbanization.
Project Objective: To strengthen sustainable regional growth by leveraging ecologically-sensitive low carbon development potential.
Phase 2: The proposed Phase 2 of the existing project - Pathway to Sustainable, Resilient and Inclusive development in Jajpur, Vyasanagar and Panasa Gram Panchayat, UN-Habitat will build on the urban sustainability assessments and the schematic designs for key urban projects prepared in Phase 1. Under the leadership of District Administration of Jajpur, UN-Habitat has completed an in-depth urban sectoral assessment including extensive spatial analyses for (i) Jajpur, (ii) Vyasanagar and (iii) Panasa Gram Panchayat. UN-Habitat’s Urban Sustainability Assessment Framework (USAF) was used to arrive at key diagnostic issues, which these urban centres are facing, namely:
• Untapped local heritage and livelihood development potential • Scattered Urban Growth • Inadequate road infrastructure and absence of public transport • Fragmented blue-green network • Vulnerable urban health
Through UN-Habitat’s ongoing work at the District, the spatially strategic plans have been developed for Jajpur, Panasa GP and Vyasanagar that address the specific diagnostic issues for the three jurisdictions as mentioned above. These strategies through specific actions and interventions provide ways for the cities and the peri-urban areas to develop with a low carbon footprint, safeguarding its rich natural assets, augmenting the quality of life of the communities and harness the untapped potential of its creative economy.
The approach for the second phase of the project is built around three components – knowledge, policy, and technical assistance. Through comprehensive activities and outputs proposed under each component, the project will create a vibrant and sustainable urban environment grounded in harnessing the cultural and heritage capital of the district.
The following would be the expected accomplishments from District Collectorate of Jajpur and UN-Habitat’s partnership under this project:
(a) Data-driven spatial urban sustainability assessment informs multi-sectoral territorial challenges and opportunities for development. (b) Low-carbon and ecologically-sensitive development pathway guided by sustainable city-district strategies (c) Improved project pipeline for demonstrable on-ground transformations (d) Strengthen local government capacity for evidence-based urban planning and management decision-making. (e) Enhanced network of local governments benefiting from knowledge products on resilient, sustainable, low-carbon development.
